I'm also running into this issue with a local model served via vLLM . I'd like to propose a practical approach for handling this case.

When the model is streaming a tool call (e.g. write), the argument chunks come in incrementally:
```text
argument: "{"
argument: "\"filePath\": \"src/app.ts\","
argument: "\"content\": \"import express..."
argument: "...more code chunks..."
argument: "...more code chunks..."
← truncated here, finish_reason: "length"
```
At this point, the tool call arguments are incomplete JSON, so OpenCode aborts the entire tool call and the partial output is lost.

Instead of aborting, OpenCode maybe should:

Detect that finish_reason is "length" while a tool call argument is still being streamed (i.e. the JSON is unclosed).
Synthetically close the incomplete JSON argument — append the necessary closing characters (", }, etc.) to make the partial argument valid.
Treat it as a completed tool call internally, but do NOT execute it (don't actually write the file).
Show a warning to the user with the partial content that was generated so far, something like:  "Tool call truncated due to output token limit. Partial content below:"
Stop the agentic loop and hand control back to the user.

This way, the user can see exactly what was generated before truncation and decide how to proceed — whether to ask the model to continue from where it left off or retry with a different approach
The key insight is: don't discard the partial streamed data. The model already generated useful content; OpenCode just needs to gracefully capture it instead of treating truncation as a fatal error.

So one workaround is that it is possible to query the internal opencode DB for the session in question and then get the last message and see if its last_finish == ‘stop’.

```nu
opencode status --session ses_2e30ba9fbffe9wtQTgcG0aGZoQ | to json
```
> {
>   "id": "ses_2e30ba9fbffe9wtQTgcG0aGZoQ",
>   "title": "Autocomplete issue in drafts with nvim headless test",
>   "slug": "mighty-mountain",
>   "version": "1.3.0",
>   "messages": 36,
>   "status": "completed",
>   "last_finish": "stop"
> }

```nu

#!/usr/bin/env nu

# OpenCode session utilities
#
# Query the local OpenCode SQLite database for session information.
# The database lives at ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.
#
# Commands:
#   opencode status - Get the status of a session by ID
#
# Examples:
#   opencode status --session ses_2e30ba9fbffe9wtQTgcG0aGZoQ

# Get the status of an OpenCode session
#
# Queries the local SQLite database to determine whether a session is
# completed, interrupted, or idle. Status is derived from the last
# assistant message's finish reason and timing data.
#
# Statuses:
#   completed    - Agent finished normally (last message finish = "stop")
#   interrupted  - Agent was mid-tool-call and stopped (finish = "tool-calls")
#   filtered     - Response was blocked by content filter
#   in-progress  - Last assistant message has no completion time (still running)
#   idle         - No assistant messages yet (user prompt with no response)
#
# Examples:
#   opencode status --session ses_2e30ba9fbffe9wtQTgcG0aGZoQ
#   opencode status --session ses_2e30ba9fbffe9wtQTgcG0aGZoQ | get status
#
# Returns: Record with session details and status
export def "opencode status" [
  --session: string  # The session ID (e.g., ses_xxx)
]: nothing -> record {
  let db = $"($env.HOME)/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db"

  let raw = (
    sqlite3 -json $db $"
      SELECT
        s.id,
        s.title,
        s.slug,
        s.version,
        s.time_created,
        s.time_updated,
        \(SELECT count\(*\) FROM message WHERE session_id = s.id\) as message_count,
        \(
          SELECT json_extract\(m.data, '$.finish'\)
          FROM message m
          WHERE m.session_id = s.id
            AND json_extract\(m.data, '$.role'\) = 'assistant'
          ORDER BY m.time_created DESC
          LIMIT 1
        \) as last_finish,
        \(
          SELECT json_extract\(m.data, '$.time.completed'\)
          FROM message m
          WHERE m.session_id = s.id
            AND json_extract\(m.data, '$.role'\) = 'assistant'
          ORDER BY m.time_created DESC
          LIMIT 1
        \) as last_completed
      FROM session s
      WHERE s.id = '($session)';
    "
  )

  if ($raw | str trim | is-empty) {
    error make { msg: $"Session ($session) not found" }
  }

  let row = ($raw | from json | first)

  let status = if ($row.last_finish | is-empty) and ($row.last_completed | is-empty) {
    "idle"
  } else if ($row.last_completed | is-empty) {
    "in-progress"
  } else if $row.last_finish == "stop" {
    "completed"
  } else if $row.last_finish == "tool-calls" {
    "interrupted"
  } else if $row.last_finish == "content-filter" {
    "filtered"
  } else {
    $"unknown \(($row.last_finish)\)"
  }

  {
    id: $row.id
    title: $row.title
    slug: $row.slug
    version: $row.version
    messages: ($row.message_count | into int)
    status: $status
    last_finish: $row.last_finish
  }
}

```

Since I posted this back in November, I kept working on my implementation. Along the way I also started optimizing OpenCode's pipeline for my own workflow — indexing, file edits, agent orchestration. The changes accumulated enough that I ended up releasing it as a standalone tool called **FastCode**. Voice input is built in as a first-class feature — `ctrl+x v` to record, or click the mic in the prompt bar. Transcribes locally with Whisper, text goes straight into the prompt. No cloud dependency for transcription. There's more beyond voice — fast apply, quick actions, work metrics, local model support — but I'll let the screenshots speak for themselves. It's live at [fastcode-dev.com](https://fastcode-dev.com) — 1 euro/month, works with cloud models or locally with Qwen 3 Coder 30B via Ollama. Thanks to everyone who upvoted and commented here. That's what pushed me to actually ship this.

For anyone looking for another option — I maintain [`opencode-claude-auth`](https://github.com/griffinmartin/opencode-claude-auth). It takes a different approach from the other plugins:

**What it does:**
- **Reads existing Claude Code credentials** — pulls OAuth tokens directly from macOS Keychain (or `~/.claude/.credentials.json` on Linux/Windows). No separate login flow
- **Multiple account support** — if you have multiple Claude Code accounts, run `opencode auth login` to switch between them. Accounts are labeled by tier (Claude Pro, Claude Max, etc.)
- **Request transforms** — handles beta headers, billing headers, system prompt identity, and tool name translation so the API accepts requests correctly
- **Auto-refresh** — if a token is near expiry, it runs the Claude CLI to refresh. Background sync every 5 minutes

**Setup** (one line in your config):

```json
{ "plugin": ["opencode-claude-auth"] }
```

Tested against OpenCode 1.3.x with 15 Anthropic models. Issues and PRs welcome on the [repo](https://github.com/griffinmartin/opencode-claude-auth).
